Get jobids required for a restore.

## Synopsis

```text
.bvfs_get_jobids [jobid=<jobid>] [ujobid=<ujobid>] [all]
```

Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Returns the chain of JobIds needed to restore the state of a job: the Full backup, the last Differential and all Incrementals up to that job, as one comma separated line. The list is the jobid= argument of the other .bvfs commands. ujobid= gives the job by its unique job name instead and takes precedence. all combines the chains of all filesets of the client.

For a Base job only its own JobId is returned. JobIds the console may not see by its job, client or fileset ACL are left out. The command only reads the catalog; the OVFS counterpart is .ovfs\_latest.

## Arguments {#arguments}

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobid=` | integer |  |  |  | Job ID. |
| `ujobid=` | string |  |  |  | Unique job name. |
| `all` | keyword |  |  |  | Every job of the chain. |

## Examples

The job chain for restoring job 628:

```text
.bvfs_get_jobids jobid=628
```

The chains of all filesets of the client:

```text
.bvfs_get_jobids jobid=628 all
```
